acquisition_method.evidence: The mass spectrometer was operated in the PRM mode to identify and quantify specific fragment ions of N-terminal peptides of human histone H3.1 and histone H4 proteins.
The mass spectrometer was operated in a data-dependent top 10 or top 15 mode.

cleavage_agent.evidence: Subsequently, protein digestion (200 ng of trypsin (Promega)) in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate was performed (overnight (ON)) and the supernatant was desalted by C18-Stagetips (reversed-phase resin) and carbon Top-Tips (Glygen) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Trypsin was chosen as specific enzyme, with 2 maximum missed cleavages allowed.

collision_energy.evidence: PRM spectra were acquired with resolution 15,000 to a target value of 2 × 105, maximum IT 60 ms, isolation window 0.7 m/z and fragmented at 27% normalized collision energy.
Peptides were fragmented by higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy of 27.

enrichment_method.evidence: experiment types: Affinity purification coupled with mass spectrometry proteomics

fractionation_method.evidence: protein bands in the molecular weight range of histones (15–23 kDa) were excised as single band/fraction.

fragmentation_method.evidence: Peptides were fragmented by higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy of 27.

labeling.evidence: Label-free quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics was used to detect and relatively quantify interaction partners of PWWP2A.
